Background

Proteins in a previous pleural fluid Olink Target 96 Inflammation pannel analysis (““GB390725-RB_pleural fluid_NPX.csv”) were observed to be outside the dynamic range of this assay. In particular, we were most confident in this behaviour for the IL6 protein abundance data, as we had independent high quality ELISA data from these same samples which showed poor correlation with the Olink measures. We believe this poor correlation was driven by the IL6 levels in our pleural samples being greatly above the dynamic range of the Olink assay.

To determine whether our pleural protein abundances were within the dynamic range of the olink assay, we re-ran a subset of 16 samples from previous pleural fluid olink inflammation analysis (““GB390725-RB_pleural fluid_NPX.csv”) in a dilution series i.e. several different concentration dilutions. From those results (see dilution-series-qc.html, we selected a 16x dilution and ran 1 plate of samples (“GB390725-RB_1_16_Extended_2026-07-06.csv”). However, from this run, qc-16x-dilution01.html, we concluded that 16x dilution still wasn’t sufficient to get IL6 in range.

However, the run 16x run of 1 plate (“GB390725-RB_1_16_Extended_2026-07-06.csv”) was performed with a bad batch of Olink reagents. So, instead of re-running plate 1 with the 64x dilution as planned, we re-ran plate 1 with a 16x dilution on the assumption that maybe the bad performance we observed was due to the reagent batch. Again, that re-run showed poor correlation with ELISA IL6. Based on this, we decided to re-run the full experiment at 64x

Key update motivating THIS analysis

These are the results from the re-run the full experiment at 64x

Purpose

This analysis aims confirm whether 64x is an appropriate/optimal dilution concentration of olink assays of pleural fluid. As it may not be possible for all Olink Target 96 Inflammation pannel protein targets to be in range, we have a set of 10 key highest priority protein targets where we would like the assay to demonstrate good performance:

IL-6, TNF, IL-8, uPA, CXCL1, IFN-γ, CXCL5, IL-17A, IL-1α, and CCL20

IL6 is our highest priority target as well as the one protein where we have independent gold standard ELISA data for comparison in matched pleural and serum samples.

QC of all measured proteins

Frequency below LOD by dilution condition

The bar chart below shows, for each protein, the number of measurements falling below the limit of detection (LOD) at each dilution level. Proteins are ordered by their total count of below-LOD values. A high frequency of below-LOD measurements at a given dilution suggests that the sample concentration may be too low for reliable quantification of that protein.
